nilReasons.documentation: A well-formed operand outside the operation's domain — the canonical case is SQRT of a negative rational.
A well-formed index or count outside the addressed collection's bounds, answered as a projection rather than a raise.
Text that does not denote a value in the operation's target encoding — NUM applied to text outside the sealed numeric grammar, or STR applied to a value with no exact lexeme.
A NIL the program wrote rather than computed: the NIL Word, or NIL inside a vector literal. Not produced by any Word's projection.
A diagnostic or structural accessor found no field to report at the position it was asked about.
A diagnostic accessor was asked for something the value does not carry — NIL-REASON applied to a value that carries no reason.

A well-formed generative operation (RANGE, FILL) whose materialized result would exceed the space water level. The only reason that projects rather than raises even for a request that could never fit.

An absence the program declared itself with ABSENT. The registered reason is this one id; the text the program gave is carried on the value as its detail and is what NIL-REASON answers, so the reason space is closed here and open there — the first parameterized reason, recorded as such.

errorCategories.documentation: A higher-order Word's block operand did not return the shape its contract requires — MAP/FILTER/FOLD/SCAN's block returned other than one value per contract.
An operation tried to redefine or delete a Core Word.

An ERROR the program raised itself with FAIL: a user Word saying that a call to it is wrong, with the program's own text as the message. The category is this one id; the text is a message, and like every message it is not a machine-readable surface.

DEF or DEL asked for a dictionary change its existing bindings refuse: DEF named a word the dictionary already binds in a way this definition cannot resolve, or DEL named a word other words still reference.

RECORD was given a key Vector in which some key appears twice. A Record holds each key once (LANG.RECORDS.STRUCTURE), and which of two values should win is a decision the program has not made, so the Word raises rather than keeping either.
The total execution-step budget was exhausted before the program finished.

A count operand is malformed for its Word's contract — TAKE or COLLECT given a count that is not a well-formed count at all (distinct from a well-formed count past the end, which TAKE projects as indexOutOfBounds); FORMAT given a digit count that is not a non-negative integer.
DEF was given a body that is not a well-formed definition: not a Vector, or an empty one.
An index operand (GET, PUT) is not a whole number.
DEF or DEL was given a name that cannot be a Word name at all (empty, wrong lexical shape).
RANGE's bounds do not describe a well-formed range (e.g. a non-finite span).
FILL's shape operand is not a well-formed shape vector.
Program text that does not parse — an unclosed block, a | outside a clause, a mismatched delimiter.
DEF was asked to define a name a live binding already holds — a name was asked to mean two things at once.
BIND was asked to bind a name that is already a Word name.

A Record Word (KEYS, VALUES, AT, WITH, WITHOUT, HAS?, MERGE) was given something other than a Record where one is required. A Record is its own domain (LANG.VALUES.DISJOINT): a Vector of pairs is not a Record and nothing converts one implicitly.
An operand the Word reads as a Scalar is not one: arithmetic on a non-number, or an order asked of something the exact order is not defined on (LT/GT, MIN/MAX, SORT/ORDER/BSEARCH).
An operand the Word reads as a String is not one, including an element of JOIN's Vector and TOKENIZE's separator.
AND, NOT, or a FILTER predicate block, met a value that is not a truth value or Unknown.
An operand the Word reads as a Vector is not one.

DEFINED? or CONTRACT was given something other than a Symbol (for CONTRACT, other than a Symbol or a block). A name is a Symbol, never a String: no Word turns text into a Symbol (LANG.DICTIONARY.ACYCLIC), so a String asking about a Word is malformed use rather than a lookup that failed.
A higher-order Word's block operand is not a CodeBlock.
DEF or DEL targeted a Core Word name, which the dictionary protects.
The native call-depth guard fired: a pathologically long acyclic call chain reached its nesting limit.
A named internal-computation ceiling other than the step budget was crossed — bigintBits, algebraicTerms, a numeric literal's digit count, or a program's byte length.
DEF was refused because the body names itself, directly or through other User words — the DEF-time acyclicity check.
Two operands of an element-wise Word have shapes that do not broadcast on some axis.
A Word was applied with fewer operands than its declared arity.

A Word that assumes its vector operand is in ascending order (BSEARCH) was given one that is not. The order is checked before the search, because a binary search over unordered data would answer something rather than nothing; that the vector is unsorted is the program being wrong about its own data, not data that did not work out.
A name in program text did not resolve to any Word in the compiled-in vocabulary or the live dictionary.
Two one-dimensional operands have different lengths where the operation requires them equal — the one-dimensional case of shapeMismatch.
DEL (or another dictionary Word) was asked to act on a name that names no Word.
